statement: A taxi charges a fixed fee plus the same amount for every mile. A $4$-mile ride costs $\$11.00$ and a $10$-mile ride costs $\$24.50$. How much does a $12$-mile ride cost?

choices.misconception: I treated the fare as proportional to distance using the 10-mile ride, 24.50 × 12 / 10 = 29.40, but the fixed fee does not grow with the distance.
I found the 2 dollar fixed fee, but then used 24.50 / 10 = 2.45 as the cost per mile, so I got 2 + 12 × 2.45 = 31.40.
I treated the fare as proportional to distance using the 4-mile ride, so a ride 3 times as long cost 11 × 3 = 33.
I added the 13.50 difference to the 10-mile fare, as if going from 10 to 12 miles cost as much as going from 4 to 10 miles.

hints: The extra money for the $10$-mile ride pays only for the extra miles.
The extra $6$ miles cost $24.50 - 11.00 = 13.50$ dollars, so each mile costs $13.50 / 6 = 2.25$ dollars.
A $12$-mile ride is $2$ miles longer than the $10$-mile ride.

solutions.reliable: Going from $4$ miles to $10$ miles adds $6$ miles and $\$13.50$, so each mile costs $\$2.25$. The fixed fee is $11.00 - 4 \cdot 2.25 = 2.00$ dollars. A $12$-mile ride costs $2.00 + 12 \cdot 2.25 = 29.00$ dollars.
solutions.elegant: Start from the $10$-mile ride and add two more miles at $\$2.25$ each: $24.50 + 4.50 = 29.00$ dollars. The fixed fee never has to be found.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
